summary: Reproduced the missing LoRARegistry release in TokenizerManager._handle_abort_req, added the matching asynchronous release, and constrained the existing 500/503 consumer fallback to release only when it still owns the same ReqState. This prevents both the reported leak and a double release when the direct-abort output is later consumed.

tests.what_was_measured: Failing-before reproduction: direct abort released the acquired LoRA ID zero times. Raw JUnit output is retained at reports/j-cbbfec46d0a2/evidence/failing-before.xml.
Passing-after focused regression and boundaries: direct LoRA abort releases once, a 503 direct-abort/consumer sequence releases exactly once, and a non-LoRA abort performs no release.
Full rid_to_state cleanup regression file after formatting: 30 tests passed and 3 subtests passed, including the independent owned-state 500 fallback boundary.
Repository formatting, lint, syntax, spelling, and registered-test policy hooks passed on the changed source and test files.
Patch whitespace and Python bytecode compilation passed.

gpu_execution_evidence: The defect and regression concern CPU-side asynchronous LoRA registry reference accounting with mocked request state; no model forward pass, kernel, or numerical GPU behavior is involved. No unrelated GPU smoke is claimed as evidence.
remaining_limitations: No live serving reproduction with model weights and a real LoRA adapter was run; validation is deterministic unit coverage of the actual TokenizerManager implementation and release coroutine calls.
No model architecture, semantic accuracy, distributed workload, or adapter eviction throughput claim is made.
The checkout is shallow at the campaign-recorded base; related upstream issue and PR state was inspected through GitHub before implementation.
